question: A federal department extended my access request because it has to consult another organization. What should the extension notice tell me?
generated_answer:
The extension notice should include the following information:

- The reason for the extension (consultation with another organization)
- The expected new deadline for responding to your request
- Information on how to contact the department for updates or to ask questions
- A statement that you have the right to file a complaint with the Information Commissioner if you are not satisfied with the extension or the handling of your request

Example:

"Dear [Your Name],

We are writing to inform you that your access request has been extended due to the need to consult with another organization. We expect to respond to your request by [new deadline].

If you have any questions or concerns, please contact us at [contact information]. You also have the right to file a complaint with the Information Commissioner if you are not satisfied with the extension or the handling of your request.

Thank you for your patience.

Sincerely,
[Department Name]"

Remember, you have the right to ask for an explanation of the extension and to request regular updates on the status of your request. If you are not satisfied with the handling of your request, you can file a complaint with the Information Commissioner.
